stories.headline: Honor's Humanoid Robot Beats Human Half-Marathon World Record in Beijing With 50:26 Time

key_facts.fact: Honor's autonomous humanoid robot 'Lightning' won the Beijing E-Town half-marathon in 50 minutes 26 seconds, faster than Jacob Kiplimo's human world record of 57:20 set in Lisbon in March 2026
key_facts.excerpt: The winner from Honor, a Chinese smartphone maker, completed the 21-kilometer (13-mile) race in 50 minutes and 26 seconds... That was faster than the human world record holder, Uganda's Jacob Kiplimo, who finished the same distance in about 57 minutes in March at the Lisbon road race.

key_facts.fact: Last year's inaugural robot half-marathon winner finished in 2 hours 40 minutes 42 seconds; this year's winning time represents a 3x improvement year-over-year
key_facts.excerpt: The performance by the robot marked a significant step forward from last year's inaugural race, during which the winning robot finished in 2 hours, 40 minutes and 42 seconds.

key_facts.fact: Participating robot teams grew from 20 last year to over 100 this year, and about 40% navigated the course autonomously rather than by remote control
key_facts.excerpt: Not only had the number of participating teams increased from 20 to more than 100, but several robot frontrunners were noticeably faster than professional athletes... nearly half of the robot entrants navigated the tougher terrain autonomously instead of being directed by remote control.

key_facts.fact: Honor (a Huawei spin-off) swept all three podium spots with self-navigated robots posting world-record-beating times; runner-up times were approximately 51 and 53 minutes
key_facts.excerpt: Teams from Honor, a Huawei spin-off, took the three podium spots, all self-navigated and posting world-record-beating times.

key_facts.fact: The winning robot had legs 90-95 cm long modeled on elite human athletes and used liquid-cooling technology adapted from Honor's smartphone division
key_facts.excerpt: Du said its robot design was modeled on outstanding human athletes, with long legs of about 95 cm (around 37 inches), and was equipped with what he called a powerful liquid-cooling system.

key_facts.fact: A remotely-controlled Honor robot crossed the finish line first at 48:19 but the autonomous-navigation winner received the championship under weighted scoring rules
key_facts.excerpt: State media outlet Global Times reported that a separate, remotely-controlled robot from Honor was the first to cross the finish line in 48 minutes and 19 seconds. But it said the winning one used autonomous navigation and received the championship under the event's weighted scoring rules.

key_facts.fact: Omdia ranked Chinese companies AGIBOT, Unitree Robotics, and UBTech as the only first-tier global vendors for general-purpose humanoid robots, each shipping over 1,000 units last year
key_facts.excerpt: London-based technology research and advisory group Omdia recently ranked three Chinese companies — AGIBOT, Unitree Robotics and UBTech Robotics Corp. — as the only first-tier vendors in its global assessment for shipment numbers for general-purpose embodied intelligent robots. They all shipped more than 1,000 units of the robots last year.

stories.headline: Tesla Launches Unsupervised Robotaxi Service in Dallas and Houston, No Safety Drivers

key_facts.fact: Tesla announced on April 18 that its robotaxi service is rolling out in Dallas and Houston, Texas, with no human driver or safety monitor in the vehicle
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla is rolling out its robotaxis in Dallas and Houston, the electric vehicle maker said on Saturday... Tesla's official robotaxi account on X announced the launch and posted two videos showing its best-selling Model Y SUVs running in the two cities with no human driver or monitor in the front seats.

key_facts.fact: Dallas and Houston join Austin and the San Francisco Bay Area as active robotaxi markets, tripling Tesla's Texas footprint
key_facts.excerpt: With Dallas and Houston now live, Texas hosts three active hubs—an impressive concentration that triples the company's Lone Star footprint in just weeks.

key_facts.fact: Tesla's H1 2026 expansion plan targets seven US cities including Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, and Las Vegas
key_facts.excerpt: The move aligns with Tesla's Q4 2025 earnings guidance, which outlined a broader H1 2026 rollout across seven U.S. cities, including Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, and Las Vegas.

key_facts.fact: Initial geofenced service areas are roughly 25 square miles per city, covering parts of Willowbrook/Jersey Village in Houston and Highland Park in Dallas
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla also shared geofence maps highlighting the initial service areas: a compact zone in Houston covering parts of Willowbrook and Jersey Village, and a similarly defined area in Dallas near Highland Park.

key_facts.fact: Much of Tesla's $1.3 trillion valuation hinges on the success of its robotaxi and FSD strategy as Musk pivots from EVs to AI and robotics
key_facts.excerpt: Expanding the robotaxi service and wider adoption of its full self-driving software, a version of which underpins the technology, is key to Tesla's growth strategy as Musk has pivoted the company's focus to artificial intelligence and robotics from EVs. Much of the company's $1.3 trillion valuation hinges on that bet.

key_facts.fact: The expansion comes as competitors Waymo and Zoox are also speeding up autonomous ride-hailing deployment
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla's move comes as the robotaxi business has regained momentum with Alphabet's Waymo and Amazon's Zoox speeding up expansion.

stories.headline: OpenAI CFO Reveals New Enterprise Model 'Spud' as Business Revenue Hits 40% of Total

key_facts.fact: OpenAI will introduce a new AI model codenamed 'Spud' for 'high-value professional work' described as the company's 'smartest model yet' with stronger reasoning and more reliable output
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says it will introduce a new artificial intelligence model for 'high-value professional work'... 'You'll see a new model coming from us in short order. We feel very excited about it,' Friar said. Codenamed Spud, OpenAI says its 'smartest model yet' offers 'stronger reasoning, better understanding of intent and dependencies, better follow-through and more reliable output in production.'

key_facts.fact: Business customers now account for 40% of OpenAI's revenue, up from 20% when CFO Sarah Friar was hired in 2024, and are expected to reach 50% by year-end
key_facts.excerpt: Friar said business customers accounted for about 20% of OpenAI's revenue when she was hired in 2024 as chief financial officer. She said it's now 40% and expected to account for half of OpenAI's sales by the end of the year.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT has more than 900 million weekly users, but approximately 95% do not pay, highlighting the need for enterprise revenue
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI boasts of more than 900 million weekly users of its core ChatGPT product, and Friar said about 95% of them 'don't pay anything' for the popular chatbot.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI shut down the Sora video generator app to redirect compute toward the new model; Friar acknowledged it was 'heartbreaking' but said they need to ensure the new model has enough compute
key_facts.excerpt: 'I think it was a little heartbreaking, but we're like, OK, it's not the main event right now,' Friar said. 'We need to make sure that our new model that's coming has enough compute.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI hired Slack CEO Denise Dresser three months ago as its first chief revenue officer to drive enterprise sales and AI agent adoption
key_facts.excerpt: Signaling that shift was the hiring three months ago of Slack CEO Denise Dresser to be OpenAI's first chief revenue officer... Dresser said she has been laser-focused on meeting with corporate leaders and positioning OpenAI as the go-to platform for workplaces employing AI agents.

key_facts.fact: Both OpenAI (valued at $852 billion) and Anthropic (valued at $380 billion) lose more money than they make and are racing toward IPOs; Anthropic now reports higher annualized revenue than OpenAI
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI, valued at $852 billion, and Anthropic, valued at $380 billion, both lose more money than they make, putting the privately-owned San Francisco-based AI research laboratories in a fierce competition to generate more revenue as they race toward becoming publicly traded on Wall Street.

stories.headline: App Releases Surge 60% YoY in Q1 Across App Store and Google Play, AI Coding Tools Suspected

key_facts.fact: New app releases across the App Store and Google Play grew 60% year-over-year in Q1 2026, according to market intelligence firm Appfigures
key_facts.excerpt: According to a new analysis from market intelligence... app releases across the App Store and Google Play grew 60% YoY in Q1.

key_facts.fact: App Store releases alone surged 80% year-over-year in Q1, outpacing the combined growth rate
key_facts.excerpt: App Store releases alone up 80%.

key_facts.fact: The surge in new app launches contradicts predictions that AI would kill the app ecosystem; instead, AI coding tools may be driving the boom by lowering barriers to app development
key_facts.excerpt: Everyone said AI would kill apps. Instead, new app launches are soaring... possibly driven by AI coding tools.

sources.title: The App Store is booming again — and AI may be why

stories.headline: Global DRAM Supply Will Meet Only 60% of Demand Through 2027 as AI Data Centers Consume Chips

key_facts.fact: DRAM manufacturers are expected to meet only 60% of global demand by end of 2027 as AI data center buildouts consume supply, according to Nikkei Asia citing industry data
key_facts.excerpt: A shortage of memory chips appears likely to continue until around 2027, with the top U.S. and South Korean suppliers raising DRAM production at a pace that will meet only about 60% of demand.

key_facts.fact: DRAM manufacturers need to increase annual production by 12% to meet demand, but current growth rate is only 7.5%, according to Counterpoint Research
key_facts.excerpt: DRAM manufacturers will have to increase their annual production by 12% between 2026 and 2027 to address this growing demand, but Counterpoint states that at the current rate, the production is only increasing by a measly 7.5%.

key_facts.fact: AI factories are pre-booking entire years' worth of DRAM supply, causing severe shortages in smartphone and PC segments; majority of new production lines focus on AI-specific HBM chips
key_facts.excerpt: AI factories are pre-booking entire year's worth of supply, leading to severe shortages in the smartphone and PC segments. And the majority of the new production lines will be focused on AI-specific DRAM such as HBM.

key_facts.fact: Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have dropped production of legacy DRAM (DDR3, DDR4, LPDDR4) to focus on higher-margin AI memory; Micron discontinued its Crucial consumer brand
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung and Co. have already dropped production of legacy DRAM such as DDR3, DDR4, and LPDDR4, further straining the market. Several companies have discontinued their OEM / PC-specific brands, Micron's Crucial is one example.

key_facts.fact: Memory is projected to reach approximately 40% of low-end smartphone manufacturing costs by mid-2026, up from 20% previously, with prices expected to rise 80-85% sequentially in Q2
key_facts.excerpt: Memory to hit ~40% of low-end smartphone manufacturing costs by mid-2026, up from 20% now.

key_facts.fact: India's smartphone shipments fell 3% YoY in Q1 2026 to a six-year low, directly attributed to AI-induced memory cost pressures forcing OEMs to hike prices
key_facts.excerpt: India's smartphone shipments fell by 3% year-on-year in the January-March period of the calendar year 2026 – marking the weakest quarter in six years – driven by artificial intelligence (AI)-induced cost pressures and device price hikes.
